applicability_by_reference: Boeing Alert Service Bulletin 737–53A1217, Revision 1, dated September 8, 2022
compliance_time: At the applicable times specified in Tables 3 through 6 of Boeing Alert Service Bulletin 737–53A1217, Revision 1, dated September 8, 2022
required_action: Perform repetitive internal and external detailed inspections, low frequency eddy current (LFEC), and medium frequency eddy current (MFEC) inspections for cracks of the skin repair of S–17, STA 360 to STA 380 and STA 888 to STA 907, left and right sides of the airplane, with corrective actions including repair if necessary.
extraction_notes: PROPOSED RULE - not in force. This is an NPRM with a comments due date of July 10, 2023. The AD applies only to Group 1 through 3, Configuration 3 airplanes as identified in Boeing Alert Service Bulletin 737–53A1217. The applicability is defined by reference to the service bulletin, which identifies which aircraft are affected.

compliance_time: Within 30 days after the effective date for inspection; replacement compliance times vary by manufacturing date: before further flight or within 15 years for 2008 or earlier; within 12 months for 2009-2010; within 24 months for 2011-2013; before exceeding 10 years or within 24 months (whichever later) for 2014 or later.
required_action: Inspect passenger chemical oxygen generators (part numbers 117080-02, 117080-03, 117080-04) to determine manufacturing date within 30 days. Replace affected generators with serviceable units according to manufacturing date-based compliance schedule. Prohibit installation of non-serviceable passenger chemical oxygen generators.
extraction_notes: This is a final rule (not proposed). The AD applies to all listed aircraft models regardless of whether they currently have the affected part numbers installed, because the generators are rotable components. Compliance times are tiered based on manufacturing date of the generators themselves, not aircraft serial numbers.

compliance_time: At the applicable times specified in the Compliance paragraph of Boeing Special Attention Requirements Bulletin 737–53–1399 RB, Revision 1, dated March 14, 2023
required_action: Perform general visual inspection for any repair, buckle, wrinkle, bulge, and cracking at skin lap splices at stringers S–4, S–14, and S–24; perform repetitive detailed inspections for buckling, wrinkling, or bulging at unrepaired areas of affected lap splices and repair; perform repetitive detailed, high frequency eddy current, and ultrasonic inspections for cracking at affected locations and repair; and perform alternative inspections and on-condition actions as specified in Boeing Special Attention Requirements Bulletin 737–53–1399 RB, Revision 1, dated March 14, 2023.
extraction_notes: AD applies to all Boeing 737-600, -700, -700C, -800, -900, and -900ER series airplanes in any category. The document notes that S–4R applies to 737–800 Boeing Converted Freighter airplanes only, and S–24R applies to 737–600, –700, –700C, 800, –900, and –900ER series airplanes only, but these are inspection location specifications within the service bulletin, not aircraft model limitations in the AD applicability. The AD itself applies to all listed models. Installation of STC ST00830SE does not affect compliance.

applicability_by_reference: Boeing Alert Service Bulletin 737–53A1217, Revision 1, dated September 8, 2022
compliance_time: At the applicable times specified in Tables 3 through 6 of paragraph 1.E., "Compliance," of Boeing Alert Service Bulletin 737–53A1217, Revision 1, dated September 8, 2022
required_action: Perform repetitive internal and external detailed inspections, low frequency eddy current (LFEC) inspections, and medium frequency eddy current (MFEC) inspections for cracks of the skin repair at Stringer S–17, and perform corrective actions if necessary.
extraction_notes: The applicability is limited to Group 1 through 3, Configuration 3 airplanes as identified in Boeing Alert Service Bulletin 737–53A1217, Revision 1, dated September 8, 2022. The AD applies to airplanes on which a repair has been accomplished at the specified locations (Stringer S–17L and S–17R, at station 360 to 380 and at station 888 to 907). The compliance time references specific tables in the incorporated service bulletin, which specify a compliance time of 50,000 total flight cycles with a grace period of 4,000 flight cycles after the repair.

applicability_by_reference: Boeing Alert Requirements Bulletin 737–25A1873 RB, dated August 25, 2023; or Boeing Alert Requirements Bulletin 737–25A1876 RB, dated September 1, 2023
compliance_time: As specified in Boeing Alert Requirements Bulletin 737–25A1873 RB (for 737-300 and -400) or 737–25A1876 RB (for 737-800), with compliance times measured from the effective date of this AD
required_action: Inspect certain galleys to determine part numbers, inspect for existing galley modification placard and marking, and replace wire bundle spiral wrap sleeving as applicable. Prohibit installation of affected galley wire bundle spiral wrap made of polyethylene with self-wrapping sleeve.
extraction_notes: PROPOSED RULE - not in force. This is an NPRM with comments due by August 9, 2024. The AD number is derived from Docket No. FAA–2024–1693. Applicability is defined by reference to two Boeing Alert Requirements Bulletins that identify which aircraft are affected. The compliance times are specified in those referenced documents and measured from the effective date of the AD (once finalized).

applicability_by_reference: Boeing 737-800BCF Airworthiness Limitations, D140A006, Revision L, dated April 1, 2021 (Section 5.2.1, Group A)
compliance_time: Before the airplane accumulates 17,000 total flight cycles, or within 5,000 flight cycles after July 17, 2019, or within 12 months after the effective date of this AD, or within 1,000 flight cycles after the effective date of this AD, whichever occurs last
required_action: Perform an ultrasonic inspection of the skin under the drag link assembly and repair tripler under the drag link assembly in accordance with Boeing Alert Service Bulletin 737-53A1368, and do all applicable on-condition actions.
extraction_notes: PROPOSED RULE - not in force. This is an NPRM with Docket No. FAA-2024-2315 and Project Identifier AD-2023-00537-T. Comments due November 12, 2024. The AD applies only to Model 737-800 series airplanes that have been converted to a freighter configuration using Boeing Drawing 800A0003 before April 1, 2021, and are identified as Group A in Section 5.2.1 of Boeing 737-800BCF Airworthiness Limitations, D140A006, Revision L. The applicability is limited by reference to Boeing 737-800BCF Airworthiness Limitations document. This AD affects and modifies AD 2019-11-06.

applicability_by_reference: Boeing Alert Requirements Bulletin 747–53A2912 RB, dated April 5, 2024
compliance_time: At the applicable times specified in the Compliance paragraph of Boeing Alert Requirements Bulletin 747–53A2912 RB, dated April 5, 2024
required_action: Inspect the fuselage skin lap splice between stations 1350 and 1480 at stringers S–23L and S–23R for cracking of the upper fastener row and perform corrective actions as specified in Boeing Alert Requirements Bulletin 747–53A2912 RB, dated April 5, 2024.

applicability_by_reference: Boeing 737-800BCF Airworthiness Limitations, D140A006, Revision L, dated April 1, 2021 (Section 5.2.1 identifies Group A airplanes affected)
compliance_time: At the compliance time specified in paragraph (g)(1)(i), (ii), (iii), or (iv), whichever occurs last: before the airplane accumulates 17,000 total flight cycles, or within 5,000 flight cycles after July 17, 2019, or within 12 months after the effective date of this AD, or within 1,000 flight cycles after the effective date of this AD. For Group 1 Configuration 1, 3, or 4: before 30,000 total flight cycles, or within 5,000 flight cycles after July 17, 2019, or within 12 months after the effective date, or within 1,000 flight cycles after the effective date.
required_action: Perform an ultrasonic inspection of the skin under the drag link assembly and repair tripler under the drag link assembly in accordance with Boeing Alert Service Bulletin 737-53A1368, dated February 27, 2018, and do all applicable on-condition actions for the inspections.
extraction_notes: This AD applies only to Model 737-800 series airplanes converted to freighter configuration using Boeing Drawing 800A0003 before April 1, 2021, and identified as Group A in Boeing 737-800BCF Airworthiness Limitations D140A006 Revision L. The applicability is limited by reference to this document which identifies specific aircraft. The AD replaces corresponding initial ultrasonic inspections and on-condition actions required by paragraph (g) of AD 2019-11-06 for these specific freighter-converted airplanes only.

compliance_time: Within 4 months after the effective date of this AD
required_action: Replace lavatory bifold door latches with part numbers SC1L500031–3/20218–3, SC1L500031–4/20218–4, SC1L500031–5/20218–5/20218–7, or SC1L500031–6/20218–6/20218–8 with latches having part numbers SC1L500031–9/20218–9 or SC1L500031–10/20218–10. Prohibit installation of affected parts.
extraction_notes: PROPOSED RULE - not in force. This is an NPRM with a comments due date of May 27, 2025. The AD number is derived from Docket No. FAA–2025–0349. Applicability is limited by part number (lavatory bifold door latch), not by aircraft serial numbers. No engine models specified. No effective date provided as this is a proposed rule.

compliance_time: As specified in EASA AD 2025-0025
required_action: Adjust the cargo swing emergency release control in accordance with EASA AD 2025-0025, with specified clarifications for distance 'B' and distance 'C' measurements.
extraction_notes: PROPOSED RULE - not in force. This is an NPRM with comments due September 5, 2025. The AD adopts EASA AD 2025-0025 with exceptions. Applicability is defined by reference to EASA AD 2025-0025. Aircraft are helicopters, not airplanes.

applicability_by_reference: Airbus Alert Operators Transmission (AOT) A32N033-24 Revision 02 (for definition of affected parts by serial number)
compliance_time: For Group 1 aeroplanes: Within 8 days or 5 flight cycles (whichever occurs later) from last inspection or before next flight after 04 August 2025 (whichever occurs later), and thereafter at intervals not to exceed 8 days or 5 flight cycles for affected MLG door 1; within 15 days after 04 August 2025 and thereafter at intervals not to exceed 8 days or 5 flight cycles for affected MLG door 2. Replacement of affected part 1 within 12 months after 22 November 2024; replacement of affected part 2 within 18 months after 04 August 2025.
required_action: Inspect main landing gear (MLG) door actuators (Part Number 114122015) with serial numbers listed in Appendix 1 Lists A and B of the AOT for jamming or inability to open. Replace affected parts with serviceable parts if discrepancies are detected or within specified timeframes. Do not install any affected parts from 04 August 2025 onwards. X-ray inspection per VSB Revision 01 or AOT Revision 03 constitutes acceptable method to accomplish replacement.
extraction_notes: This is Revision 2 of EASA AD 2025-0158. The AD defines affected parts by Part Number (114122015) and serial numbers listed in external documents (AOT Appendix 1 Lists A and B), not by aircraft MSN ranges. All aircraft MSN are covered. The applicability is limited to specific part serial numbers, which are component serial numbers (not aircraft MSN), so serial_ranges remains empty per instructions. The applicability_by_reference field references the AOT document which defines which specific part serial numbers are affected.

compliance_time: Before exceeding the threshold and thereafter at intervals as defined in Table 1, depending on aeroplane group and zone. Thresholds range from 19,500 flight cycles since first flight or last repair to 3 months after 10 November 2025 (original issue date). Inspection intervals range from 500 to 2000 flight cycles depending on group and zone.
required_action: Accomplish Special Detailed Inspection (SDI) of each zone (A, B, C) of the 80 VU rack attachments in accordance with Airbus Service Bulletin A320-25-1BKJ Revision 04 or A320-25-1CJH Revision 01, as applicable. If discrepancies are detected, accomplish applicable corrective actions per the SB. Report inspection results to Airbus within 90 days.
extraction_notes: This is Revision 01 of AD 2025-0237, issued 23 June 2026 with correction date 24 June 2026. The original issue was 10 November 2025. The AD applies to all manufacturer serial numbers (no serial number restrictions). Compliance thresholds and intervals are complex and vary by aeroplane group (1-5) and zone (A, B, C), as detailed in Table 1. Group definitions depend on embodiment of specific modifications and service bulletins. The AD references two applicable service bulletins: A320-25-1BKJ Revision 04 (for CEO aeroplanes, Groups 1-4) and A320-25-1CJH Revision 01 (for NEO aeroplanes, Group 5). Later approved revisions of these documents are acceptable.

compliance_time: Within 6 months after 06 November 2025 for replacement of affected parts with serial numbers listed in Appendix 1; within 24 months after 06 November 2025 for inspection of affected parts with serial numbers not listed in Appendix 1; from the effective date of this AD, affected parts may be installed if they pass inspection concurrently with installation.
required_action: Replace fire panels with affected part numbers and serial numbers listed in Appendix 1 within 6 months; inspect fire panels with affected part numbers but serial numbers not listed in Appendix 1 within 24 months; do not install affected parts with serial numbers listed in Appendix 1 unless repaired and reinspected as applicable; all installations of affected parts must pass inspection concurrently with installation.
extraction_notes: This is Revision 01 of EASA AD 2025-0274, issued 07 July 2026, effective 14 July 2026. It supersedes the original EASA AD 2025-0274 dated 09 December 2025 (including its correction dated 11 December 2025), which in turn superseded EASA AD 2025-0253 dated 14 November 2025. The AD addresses fire panel inspection and replacement requirements for Airbus A318, A319, A320, and A321 aircraft. Applicability is limited to specific fire panel part numbers (700TS06Y, 700TS06Y10, 700TS06Y11, 700TS06Y111, 700TS06Y12, 330TS08Y, 335TS08Y00, 335TS08Y01) and specific serial numbers listed in Appendix 1. The compliance requirements are complex and differentiated by whether the aircraft is Group 1 (has affected part installed) or Group 2 (does not have affected part installed or received after 11 September 2025 without affected parts installed after that date).

compliance_time: For Group 1 aeroplanes: within 36 months after 11 March 2026. For Group 2 aeroplanes: do not install affected slides after 11 March 2026.
required_action: Replace each affected evacuation slide with a serviceable slide in accordance with Airbus Service Bulletin A320-25-1CML or A320-25-1CMM. Do not install affected slides on any aeroplane.
extraction_notes: This is a revision (R1) of EASA AD 2026-0037. Applicability is limited to specific aircraft models (all variants listed) with all manufacturer serial numbers. The AD defines affected slides and affected hoses by part number and serial number ranges in the Definitions section and Appendix 1. Group 1 aeroplanes are those with affected slides installed; Group 2 aeroplanes are those without affected slides. The compliance time differs by group: Group 1 must replace within 36 months; Group 2 must not install affected slides after the effective date. Serial number ranges for affected slides are defined in Appendix 1 (e.g., D31516-XXX prior to s/n M11767, C1745, L25862, A17696). These are component serial numbers, not aircraft MSNs, so serial_ranges is left empty per instructions.

compliance_time: Within compliance time as identified in Table 1 (threshold A, B, C, D, E or F, whichever occurs later), then at intervals as defined in Table 2. Threshold A is before exceeding 21,100 flight cycles since aeroplane first flight; Threshold B is within 17,300 FC since accomplishment of the MSB; Threshold C is within 3,150 FC after accomplishment of first rework; Threshold D is within 12,400 FC after accomplishment of second or third rework; Threshold E is within 890 FC after last accomplishment before effective date of ALI task 531105-01-2; Threshold F is within 3,150 FC after last accomplishment before effective date of ALI task 531105-02-2.
required_action: Accomplish High Frequency Eddy Current (HFEC) inspection of horizontal upper stiffeners of lateral window frame at fuselage Frame 4 (both RH and LH sides) in accordance with Airbus Service Bulletin A320-53-1544 or A320-53-1545, as applicable. If discrepancies are detected, accomplish applicable corrective actions in accordance with the inspection SB before next flight.
extraction_notes: Applicability excludes aeroplanes on which Airbus modifications 165961, 162338, or 162339 were embodied in production. All manufacturer serial numbers are affected except those with the listed modifications. The AD includes complex compliance thresholds based on aircraft history (flight cycles, prior rework, prior modifications, and prior ALI task accomplishments). Repetitive inspection intervals vary based on affected part configuration (5,200 FC, 3,150 FC, or 2,400 FC depending on modification/rework status). Compliance times for LH and RH sides may differ per Note 1.

applicability_by_reference: Airbus Service Bulletin A320-92-1116 Revision 02 or A320-92-1118 Revision 01
compliance_time: Within 4 months after effective date for initial GVI of affected parts (Group 1); thereafter at intervals not exceeding 4 months. Before next flight after hard landing or severe turbulence. Within 24 months for detailed inspection to identify manufacturer. Before next flight for replacement of affected parts if identified as "SA" manufacturer.
required_action: Accomplish repetitive general visual inspections (GVI) of battery retaining rods on Group 1 aeroplanes (those with affected parts installed). Within 24 months, perform detailed inspection to identify manufacturer. Replace affected battery retaining rods with serviceable parts if found broken or if identified as "SA" manufacturer quality marked parts.
extraction_notes: AD applies to all MSN of listed aircraft models. Applicability is limited to Group 1 aeroplanes (those with affected battery retaining rods P/N D9241023700000 installed) for most inspection and replacement requirements. Group 2 aeroplanes (those without affected parts) have limited applicability only for parts installation (paragraph 8). The affected part definition is complex: P/N D9241023700000 rods are affected unless they lack "SA" quality marking/designation or have been identified with applicable SB label. Serviceable parts are new rods or any rod eligible for installation that is not an affected part.

compliance_time: Initial inspection compliance times vary by aircraft model and accumulated flight cycles/hours at the effective date (22 July 2026), ranging from before exceeding 30,000 FC or 60,000 FH to within 2,500 FC or 5,000 FH after the effective date. Thereafter, repetitive inspections at intervals not to exceed 6,950 FC or 13,900 FH, whichever occurs first.
required_action: Accomplish repetitive rototest inspections of the forward pressure bulkhead hole C1 at Frame 35 (or Frame 35.8 for A321) at Stringer 30 on both sides in accordance with the inspection service bulletin. If cracks are detected, contact Airbus for approved repair instructions before next flight. Modification of the affected areas in accordance with the modification service bulletin constitutes terminating action for the repetitive inspections.
extraction_notes: Applicability excludes certain aircraft with specific modifications already embodied: A318 with mod 39195 or SB A320-00-1219; A319 CEO with mods 28238, 28162, 28342; A319 NEO with mod 162338; A320 NEO with mod 162339; and all aircraft with mod 174066. All manufacturer serial numbers are affected except those with the listed modifications. No engine models specified. Compliance times are complex and depend on accumulated flight cycles/hours at the effective date, with different tables for A318 versus A319/A320/A321.

compliance_time: For Group 1 aeroplanes: before next flight after 29 November 2025. For Group 2 aeroplanes: from 29 November 2025, do not modify any aeroplane into a Group 1 aeroplane. AFM update within 7 days after the effective date of this AD.
required_action: Replace each affected ELAC (ELAC B L104) with a serviceable ELAC (ELAC B L103+ or any subsequent eligible ELAC) in accordance with Airbus AOT or Service Bulletin instructions. After modification, do not install an affected ELAC. Amend the AFM in accordance with Airbus FOT instructions.
extraction_notes: This AD supersedes EASA AD 2025-0268-E. The applicability defines two groups of aeroplanes with different compliance requirements: Group 1 (those with affected configuration on 29 November 2025) must replace the ELAC before next flight after that date; Group 2 (all others) must not be modified into Group 1 configuration from that date forward. All serial numbers are affected. The AD references specific part numbers for affected and serviceable ELACs and provides alternative compliance methods via Service Bulletins or other Airbus-approved instructions.

compliance_time: Before accumulating 22 years after THSA first flight, or within 3 months after 21 September 2012, whichever occurs later, and thereafter at intervals not exceeding 24 months for repetitive inspections. If corrosion is found, accomplish corrective actions within the applicable compliance time as defined in the Service Bulletin.
required_action: Accomplish detailed inspections of the ballscrew lower splines of affected Trimmable Horizontal Stabilizer Actuators (THSA) to detect corrosion, and if corrosion is found, perform corrective actions including additional inspections and replacement of the affected THSA. Do not install affected THSA parts unless they have not accumulated 22 years since first flight or are determined to be Type 1 (no corrosion).

compliance_time: Within the threshold specified in Table 1 or Table 2 (whichever occurs later), and thereafter at intervals not exceeding 500 flight cycles or 1,000 flight hours (whichever occurs first), perform repetitive detailed visual inspections. Accomplish a special detailed inspection within the threshold specified in Table 3.
required_action: Perform repetitive detailed visual inspections of Main Landing Gear support rib 5 at specified intervals, and accomplish a one-time special detailed inspection of the lug bore holes as terminating action. If discrepancies are detected, contact Airbus for approved corrective instructions before next flight.
extraction_notes: The Applicability section specifies aircraft having MSN "listed in the Appendix 1 of this AD." Appendix 1 contains a specific list of affected MSNs ranging from 04963 to 09495. Not all MSNs in this range are affected—only those explicitly listed in Appendix 1. However, per the extraction rules, serial_ranges should reflect the continuous range of MSNs that appear in the affected list. The AD applies only to aircraft with the specific MSNs listed in Appendix 1, not all aircraft with MSNs between 4963 and 9495. The affected parts are identified by Part Number and serial number in Appendix 1; these are component serial numbers, not aircraft MSNs, but the aircraft applicability is limited by the MSN list provided.

compliance_time: Within 15 days after 28 July 2026 to determine rudder serial number; before exceeding 2,000 flight cycles or 12 months (whichever first) since aeroplane reference date, or concurrently with first rudder removal after 28 July 2026 (whichever first) to accomplish inspections; corrective actions within compliance time specified in Service Bulletin if discrepancies detected.
required_action: Visually inspect rudder to determine serial number; accomplish detailed visual inspection and woodpecker inspection of affected rudder areas per Airbus Service Bulletin A320-55-1070; perform corrective actions if discrepancies are detected; report rudder serial number and aeroplane MSN to Airbus within 15 days; report inspection results to Airbus within 30 days.
extraction_notes: This is Revision 01 of EASA AD 2026-0144, issued 11 September 2026, superseding the original issue dated 28 July 2026. The applicability is limited to seven specific aircraft MSNs (12680, 12729, 12751, 12764, 12776, 12852, 12912) with specific rudder serial numbers listed in Appendix 1. The AD addresses dents on rudder outer skin caused by storage trolleys during assembly. Compliance times reference both the original effective date (28 July 2026) and the revision effective date (18 September 2026).

compliance_time: For Group 1 aeroplanes: within 4 months after 20 July 2026 for initial GVI, then at intervals not to exceed 4 months; before next flight after hard landing or severe turbulence; within 24 months after 20 July 2026 for detailed inspection of battery support assemblies and replacement of affected parts. For Group 2 aeroplanes: from effective date, installation of affected parts allowed if new and identified with label within 24 months after 20 July 2026.
required_action: Accomplish general visual inspection (GVI) of battery retaining rods at specified intervals and before next flight after hard landing or severe turbulence; perform detailed inspection of battery support assemblies to identify manufacturer; replace affected battery retaining rods with serviceable parts or identify with label as applicable; allow installation of new affected parts only if identified with label within 24 months.
extraction_notes: This AD addresses battery retaining rod failures due to manufacturing defects. Applicability is limited to specific aircraft with affected parts (Part Number D9241023700000 manufactured by SUDAERO or unknown supplier) that lack "SA" quality marking/designation. The AD defines two groups: Group 1 (aeroplanes with affected parts installed, except those with Airbus modification 162321) and Group 2 (all others). Different compliance requirements apply to each group. The AD supersedes EASA AD 2026-0130 and retains most of its requirements while amending applicability, group definitions, extending compliance times, and providing relabelling instructions.
